rationale: THE IMPORTED VALUE RECEIVER (2026-11-25). A receiver root this file binds through `import` names a VALUE whose type the DECLARING file states; this pass sees the binding but not the declaration, so it has no member set to resolve `run` inside. The honest answer is to WITHDRAW the row via `typescriptUnresolvedReceiver`, which makes the store drop the name binding. Without it the row fell to the store's tie-break and bound to a SAME-NAMED member in a third file — MEASURED on a three-file repro: `workerInstance.run()`, imported from a file where the value is a `Worker`, bound to `other.ts:run`, a class the caller never imports and whose `run` the value cannot be. The import specifier here resolves to nothing on disk, which is exactly the shape under test: a binding whose type is NOT in this file. `Other` is load-bearing — it makes `run` ambiguous so the name model has something wrong to pick. The pin is `owner: null` PLUS the withdrawal flag: null alone would also pass a row that simply never resolved, which is why the flag is asserted separately.

expectRelationships.note: THE CONTRACT: no owner, and the explicit withdrawal that tells the store not to tie-break by name

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT: a cross-file misbinding to a class the caller never imports
THE PRE-FIX SHAPE: no withdrawal, so the store's name model decides the binding
